entries.title: Nepal says it will need billions in funding to rebuild after flash floods
entries.snippet: BBC South Asia correspondent Azadeh Moshiri is in Nepal where authorities are trying to begin rebuilding amid the debris.

entries.title: Tensions flare as judge declines to remove juror in Lindsay Clancy trial

entries.title: Argentina to sanction oil firms as tensions heighten in Falklands dispute with UK
entries.snippet: Javier Milei reiterates his country's claim on the British overseas territory, saying the "winds of change" favour it.

entries.title: US investigating if missile hit Iran wedding, Vance says
entries.snippet: The Iranian Red Crescent Society (IRCS) said shrapnel from a missile hit the ceremony and killed four people on Tuesday.

entries.title: Steve Irwin's family celebrates 'superhero' dad, 20 years after shock death
entries.snippet: The Australian icon was killed in 2006, after a stingray's barb pierced his chest during filming.

entries.title: Transplanted pig kidney works in US man's body for record 271 days
entries.snippet: A man has lived for a record nine months with a transplanted pig kidney while waiting for a human transplant.

entries.title: UN warns of 'supersized' El Niño as countries prepare for impact
entries.snippet: The WMO has warned that the natural weather phenomenon could bring disruption to global economies.

entries.title: Around 2,000 fall ill in Indonesia after eating free school meals
entries.snippet: Authorities are investigating several suspected outbreaks amid growing criticism of the scheme.

entries.title: US billionaire Leon Black defies summons and sues Epstein panel
entries.snippet: The lawsuit calls the House Oversight Committee's subpoenas, which ordered him to share nondisclosure agreements, "invalid".

entries.title: Feminist activist and journalist Gloria Steinem dies, aged 92
entries.snippet: Her foundation said she "passed away peacefully" at her home in New York City, "surrounded by many who loved her".

entries.title: Volkswagen board approves plan to cut another 50,000 jobs
entries.snippet: The group - which includes Audi, Porsche, Skoda as well as the VW brand - plans to cut a total of 100,000 by 2030.

entries.title: Palestinian teens killed during settler attack on West Bank village, officials say
entries.snippet: Al-Mughayyir's council says they were trying to stop settlers stealing sheep, but the Israeli military says they threw stones at its troops.

entries.title: 'Beautiful, vibrant' Disney star Carla Jeffery dies aged 33
entries.snippet: Jeffery was known for playing cheerleader Bree in 2018 Disney Channel movie Zombies and two sequels.

entries.title: ICE agent charged with lying about shooting Venezuelan man during crackdown
entries.snippet: The ICE officer faces federal charges related to the January shooting in Minnesota.

entries.title: More than 80 migrants feared dead after boat rescued off Canary Islands
entries.snippet: Rescuers found 44 survivors on board the vessel but bad weather meant they had to leave five bodies behind.

entries.title: Anthony Joshua's driver attempted overtake before fatal crash, trial hears
entries.snippet: Adeniyi Mobolaji Kayode is charged in Nigeria with offences including causing death by dangerous driving.

entries.title: Embattled Spanish PM insists there were no prior warnings before Ceuta crisis
entries.snippet: Pedro Sánchez tells parliament it is absurd to think the government knew and did nothing, after thousands join protests in Spanish cities.

entries.title: Trump $1 coin makes him first living president on US currency in a century
entries.snippet: The US Mint special edition is stamped with a portrait of Trump alongside the words "LIBERTY" and "IN GOD WE TRUST"

entries.title: Vance's Antichrist comments are a 'common belief', his friend tells BBC
entries.snippet: The US vice-president recently mused with a Christian podcast host on whether the end of the world was nigh.

entries.title: Girl group Katseye are missing two members, but their tour still dazzles
entries.snippet: Reduced but resilient, girl group Katseye received a hero's welcome in London.

entries.title: The Trump administration still aims to make state citizenship lists ahead of midterms
entries.snippet: The Trump administration is taking the unprecedented step of creating lists of adult citizens who are eligible to vote in each state – but will not meet its own deadline 60 days before Election Day.

entries.title: Leon Black defies subpoena to testify in Epstein inquiry and sues House panel
entries.snippet: The billionaire investor is under two subpoenas from the House Oversight Committee. But in his lawsuit, Black says the panel doesn't have the authority to compel him to share nondisclosure agreements.

entries.title: Trump asks Supreme Court to lift block on USPS plan to restrict mail voting
entries.snippet: The Trump administration has asked the Supreme Court to lift a temporary block on the U.S. Postal Service plan for President Trump's attempt to restrict mail-in voting for the midterm election.

entries.title: Tributes to Gloria Steinem are flooding in, from Hollywood to Capitol Hill
entries.snippet: Women in politics and pop culture are paying tribute to Gloria Steinem after her death at 92. Many called her not only an inspiration but a friend.

entries.title: Later in life, Gloria Steinem found herself free of the 'demands of gender'
entries.snippet: In 2015, the trailblazing feminist told Fresh Air she that had entered a new phase in life, one in which "you can do what you want." Steinem died Sept. 2 at the age of 92.

entries.title: ICE officer faces federal charges for lying over shooting of Venezuelan immigrant
entries.snippet: The charges represent a rare moment of the Justice Department seeking to hold immigration officers accountable.

entries.title: Fox News abruptly parts ways with scandal-tarred star Maria Bartiromo
entries.snippet: Fox News abruptly announced it had cut ties with anchor Maria Bartiromo after more than a dozen years.

entries.title: Kissing apes, anti-splash urinals: This year's Ig Nobels showcase surprising science
entries.snippet: The Ig Nobel Prizes were awarded this week for humorous yet thought-provoking research. This year, the ceremony came with a twist.

entries.title: Dems demand DHS fund election security. And, journalist Gloria Steinem has died
entries.snippet: Two Democrats are demanding that Homeland Security officials fund election security ahead of the midterms. And, trail-blazing journalist Gloria Steinem has died.

entries.title: Gloria Steinem, trailblazing journalist and activist, dies at 92
entries.snippet: At a time when women were largely limited to domestic roles, Steinem challenged gender stereotypes and championed feminist ideals like equality, sisterhood and reproductive freedom.

entries.title: Fed governor Waller muddies outlook on possible rate hike later this month
entries.snippet: Federal Reserve governor Christopher Waller said Thursday that an inflation report next week will largely determine whether he supports an interest rate hike later this month or not.

entries.title: Proud of their oil, Venezuelans view major U.S. stake in their reserves as a surrender
entries.snippet: A troubled nation's pride took a bruising last week when acting President Delcy Rodríguez agreed to give the United States control of roughly one-fifth of Venezuela's oil reserves – the largest in the world.

entries.title: Global warming will exceed 1.5-degree limit, UN says in report that maps path back below danger zone
entries.snippet: In a strategic retreat in the fight against climate change, the United Nations has acknowledged that Earth has lost its chance to prevent some of the worst of global warming's harms. So now the world must figure out how to get temperatures below the danger zone and back to safety

entries.title: Remembering Gloria Steinem and her trailblazing fight for women's rights

entries.title: Trump appointees advance plans for Lafayette Square fencing and White House gates
entries.snippet: Pieces of President Donald Trump's wide-ranging Washington makeover made their next step toward approval Thursday, but not without substantial critiques of plans for permanent fencing and gates around Lafayette Square in front of the White House.

entries.title: Steinem stayed true to herself despite intense pressure, Julie Taymor says
entries.snippet: To discuss the life and legacy of Gloria Steinem, Amna Nawaz spoke with Julie Taymor. She's the director of the 2020 film "The Glorias," a biopic that spans eight decades of Steinem's life.

entries.title: Maria Bartiromo out at Fox News after more than a decade; no reason specified for departure
entries.snippet: Fox News Media has parted ways with politically influential financial journalist Maria Bartiromo after more than a decade, the company announced Thursday hours after Fox Business Network aired the final episode of the show that bears her name.

entries.title: Russia may force more men to fight in Ukraine as military faces heavy losses
entries.snippet: With Russian military losses estimated at some 40,000 a month, there are signs the Kremlin is preparing for the possibility of a much broader call-up, perhaps after parliamentary elections later this month. Special correspondent Simon Ostrovsky reports.

entries.title: NBA hits LA Clippers with a record fine for circumventing salary cap
entries.snippet: The NBA handed out one of its harshest penalties ever against the Los Angeles Clippers for circumventing the salary cap with star forward Kawhi Leonard. The league suspended the team's owner, stripped draft picks and fined the Clippers $30 million. William Brangham discussed more

entries.snippet: Most professional football players gain fans and win fame from what they do during the game. In the case of rookie offensive lineman Shiyazh Pete, millions came to know him from what he said afterward. Pete, the first Navajo player to sign an NFL contract, was invited by the coac

entries.snippet: The history of Islamophobia in the U.S. dates back decades, from FBI surveillance of Muslim and Arab communities in the 1960s to the sweeping surveillance programs launched after 9/11. Journalist Rozina Ali traces that history in her new book, "Seasons of Fury: Four Families and

entries.title: Scientists studying cockroach milk, nose-blowing win 2026 Ig Nobel prizes for quirky science
entries.snippet: Ten research teams were honored Thursday at a satirical science awards ceremony that was hosted outside the U.S. for the first time due to travel concerns.

entries.title: Democrats promise a big agenda if they win control of Congress, but their unity is being tested
entries.snippet: Beginning on Day One, House Democrats plan to "hold the crooks accountable." That's the promise House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries has made, previewing an ambitious agenda if Democrats seize majority control from Republicans in the midterm elections.

entries.title: EPA proposal could leave the public in the dark on data center plans
entries.snippet: A plan by the Environmental Protection Agency could make it harder for the public to learn about and comment on proposed AI data centers that have sparked backlash in communities across the United States and transformed the midterm election landscape.

entries.title: WATCH: Vance holds White House briefing after Leavitt's departure
entries.snippet: White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt has left the White House and President Donald Trump has yet to name a replacement. So Vice President JD Vance stepped in Thursday to brief the media.

entries.title: Federal judge considers whether to extend ban against U.S. Postal Service mail voting changes
entries.snippet: U.S. District Court Judge Indira Talwani is deciding whether to extend her prohibition on the proposed regulation of mail ballots, an effort undertaken as part of an executive order by President Donald Trump.

entries.title: Trump promises to campaign for Republicans and says they have a winning midterm message
entries.snippet: Voters' dim views of the economy and the war in Iran have put Republicans in a tough spot as the midterm election season enters its final stretch.

entries.title: DW
entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: FIFA accuses UEFA of 'smear campaign' against Infantino
entries.snippet: The dispute between the two football associations reached a US court, in which UEFA is looking for permission to collect evidence for criminal proceedings in Switzerland.

entries.title: Volkswagen to cut 100,000 jobs by end of decade
entries.snippet: The company will carry out the biggest job cuts ever seen in the industry. Volkswagen also plans to restructure and invest in research.

entries.title: Berlin: BER Airport Terminal 1 reopened after security scare
entries.snippet: Police have given the all-clear at Terminal 1 at Berlin's BER Airport following an earlier security scare and evacuation. The airport said some flights had been delayed but they were trying to avoid any cancelations.

entries.title: Israel releases first of 5 Lebanese prisoners
entries.snippet: Israel has agreed to release five civilians in exchange for Lebanese assistance in locating the bodies of missing Lebanese Jewish leaders killed in the 1980s. Talks aimed at ending the war with Hezbollah remain stalled.

entries.title: Indonesia: Thousands fall sick from free school meals
entries.snippet: Hundreds of new food poisoning cases have been reported this week linked to President Prabowo Subianto's free school lunch program. The costly scheme has been dogged by health concerns and allegations of corruption.

entries.title: Trump's Iran strategy: Could this become a forever war?
entries.snippet: The US has launched fresh attacks on military targets in Iran. It wants to prevent Tehran rebuilding its destroyed capabilities, but risks triggering a sustained downward spiral of reconstruction followed by new attacks.

entries.title: Norway seizes Russian ship in Svalbard to compensate Ukraine
entries.snippet: Authorities in Norway have seized a Russian ship, the Professor Molchanov, on a court order sought and obtained by Naftogaz in Ukraine. Russia has protested the move, which stems from its refusal to pay Naftogaz damages.

entries.title: Germany: From emigration to immigration destination
entries.snippet: Migration is a sensitive topic in Germany, with public debate dominated by the fear of uncontrolled immigration. People forget that, over two centuries, millions of Germans emigrated in search of a better life.

entries.title: US sanctions halt TOEFL and GRE tests in Iran, disrupting study plans
entries.snippet: Students in Iran can no longer take English-language proficiency exams after the suspension of a US sanctions exemption. Applicants say the move threatens university deadlines and adds costly travel obligations.

entries.title: Putin denies fresh mobilization campaign in Ukraine war
entries.snippet: The Russian president said there was no present need to mobilize more men, describing the reports as Ukrainian "disinformation." Putin was speaking during an economic forum in Russia's east.

entries.title: Can Hichilema heal Zambia's political divide?
entries.snippet: The Zambian president starts a second term after a contested election exposed deep political divisions. His challenge now is to unite the country while addressing concerns over political freedoms.

entries.title: Nvidia to buy Hugging Face in $12.93 billion deal
entries.snippet: The AI chip maker said it would keep Hugging Face an open platform that would not require developers to use Nvidia hardware.

entries.title: South Africa airline behind viral stadium flyby scraps repeat display
entries.snippet: Two passenger jets passed close to Cape Town's DHL Stadium during a flyover last weekend. The carrier said it has shelved plans to repeat the display as South Africa's aviation authority investigates the event.

entries.title: Is Germany's economic slump finally over?
entries.snippet: Despite a slew of negative headlines, the German economy has posted its best figures in years. There are reasons for optimism, but structural issues remain.

entries.title: Malaysia's middle path between China and US faces new tests
entries.snippet: The prime minister's comments on Taiwan and US-backed military facilities near Sabah have revived questions over Malaysia's non-aligned foreign policy.

entries.title: Iran bets on shadow networks to evade US sanctions
entries.snippet: To circumvent US sanctions, Iran has spent decades building a complex network of businesspeople and companies. A billionaire once sentenced to death is now back at its center.

entries.title: India news: Jaishankar offers help to end war in Ukraine
entries.snippet: Foreign Minister S. Jaishankar says India is prepared to assist efforts to end the war in Ukraine, as the foreign minister visits Kyiv. DW has more.

entries.title: Gloria Steinem, feminist activist and journalist, dies at 92
entries.snippet: Steinem became a prominent leader of the second wave of the feminist movement in the US.

entries.title: 'Supersized' El Nino could be strongest on record, UN says
entries.snippet: The current El Nino could end up being the strongest since records began 40 years ago, the UN warns. It says the phenomenon is being "supersized" thanks to exceptionally warm temperatures in the tropical Pacific Ocean.
